title: Investigate microbatch hysteresis and memory‑strided regressions introduced by FlashAttention v3 layout changes
creator: Lena Rodriguez
description:
Background: After integrating FlashAttention v3 kernels into the serving runtime, we've observed intermittent latency spikes and reduced throughput for short-sequence prefill workloads. Initial profiling shows higher memory striding and write amplification during KV cache population in certain microbatch sizes. This issue appears as a hysteresis effect: throughput recovers after a steady-state warmup but regressions occur during bursty traffic and during canary rollouts that mix v2 and v3 kernels.

Goals:
- Identify the root cause(s) in the v3 memory layout and the scheduler interaction that lead to microbatch hysteresis.
- Produce reproducible perf tests that expose the regression across GPU generations (A100, H100).
- Implement mitigations: scheduling heuristic changes, microbatch hysteresis damping, or temporary v3 layout shims.
- Provide a safe rollout plan and rollback gates for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope & out‑of‑scope:
- In scope: kernel selection logic, prefill/decode scheduling interaction, KV cache write patterns, and conservative mitigations in the runtime.
- Out of scope: upstream FlashAttention codebase rewrite (we will coordinate with model/ML partners if necessary).
acceptance_criteria: Identify minimal reproducer and publish a benchmark script with exact traffic patterns that trigger the hysteresis
Pin the dominant allocation/writes in the kernel path with perf & CUPTI traces and map to source lines
Propose at least two mitigation strategies with cost/latency tradeoffs and prototype one in the runtime
Demonstrate mitigation reduces transient P99 latency by >=30% on representative prefill workloads and keeps throughput within 5% of baseline
Define rollout gates and automated checks for canary (latency regression <5% over 1h with 99th perc sampling)
implementation_plan: Triage: reproduce locally using the perf harness and our serving canary images (2d)
Profiling: collect NVTX/CUPTI traces, heap dumps, and kernel occupancy maps (2d)
Hypotheses: enumerate candidate causes (layout stride, misaligned memcpy, allocator fragmentation, scheduler preemption) (1d)
Prototype: implement a scheduler patch that adds microbatch hysteresis damping and an optional v3 layout shim to reduce write stride (3d)
Test: run multi-GPU perf topo matrix and long-run soak tests on Dedicated pool (2d)
Rollout: canary to 5% of hosted traffic -> monitor -> ramp to 50% -> full (with rollback on gate)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shim reduces v3 memory/compute benefits. Mitigation: make shim opt-in and gated by model-profile; measure cost delta per-model.
Risk: Scheduler changes increase tail latency for long-sequence decode. Mitigation: add heuristic that toggles behavior by sequence-length distribution and warmup state.
Risk: Repro requires specific infra. Mitigation: create a self-contained perf harness and publish to the team drive with reproducible container images.
qa_and_validation: Add automated benchmark to CI that runs the reproducer at multiple concurrency points and fails on P99 > baseline + 20%
Manual verification on Dedicated test pool across A100/H100 images
Compare model output quality metrics (tokens per second, latency) to ensure no functional regressions
